4289.title: Adolf en Catharina Croeser, bekend als ‘De burgemeester van Delft en zijn dochter’
4289.creator: Unknown

editorial.note: Wijdbeens, met de hand in de zij, zit Croeser op de stoep van zijn huis aan de Oude Delft in Delft. Zijn dertienjarige dochter Catharina kijkt ons recht aan.
Op een open veranda zingt en speelt een jongeman op zijn luit. Het is niet duidelijk waar de juffrouw naast hem met haar gedachten is.
Het schilderij weigert zijn geheimen prijs te geven. De voorstelling wordt gezien als een aansporing om God te loven met zang en snarenspel, maar ook als een scabreuze verleidingsscène.

Een jonge tekenleerling krijgt instructies van zijn meester in diens schildersatelier. Misschien is de meester Abraham van Strij zelf, die samen met zijn broer Jacob een grote werkplaats in Dordrecht had.

4733.title: Een moeder die haar kind pap voert
4733.creator: Unknown

editorial.note: Een moeder die haar kind pap voert. Een zittende vrouw voert met een lepel uit een aardewerken kom pap aan een staand kind.

Een jonge vrouw speelt, in een voornaam interieur, op het virginaal. Op het deksel van het instrument is een landschap geschilderd met een intiem wandelend stelletje. Muziek brengt mensen samen – nodigt de muzikante uit om mee te spelen?

Stilleven met muziekinstrumentem, vaatwerk en fruit. Links een cister, een luit, een cello, een viool, een doedelzak, een trompet of hoorn, een fluit en bladmuziek. Op tafel liggen verschillende bokalen, schalen en borden.

151696.title: Isaac and Rebecca, Known as ‘The Jewish Bride’
151696.creator: Rembrandt van Rijn

editorial.note: To prevent being killed and having his wife captured by King Abimelech, Isaac concealed his love for Rebecca by pretending they were brother and sister. However, their intimacy betrayed them when they thought they were not being spied on.

151703.title: Tobit and Anna with the Kid
151703.creator: Rembrandt van Rijn

editorial.note: Tobit’s blindness has condemned him and his wife to a life of grinding poverty: his once expensive tabard is torn and tattered. When Anna comes home with a kid, a reward for her hard work, Tobit thinks she has stolen it.
The entire family is in high spirits, creating a ruckus: father, mother, and grandmother sing loudly, the children join in, and they even puff on long pipes.

In this night scene – a novelty in painting at the time – Vermeyen succeeded in creating a dramatic effect. Candlelight plays over the faces and casts dark shadows. For the flames, Vermeyen used gold leaf.
Van Mieris demonstrates his superb artistry in this painting. The dazzling array of materials and textures is a feast for the eyes.
The seated woman tries to entice the young man by offering him rosebuds. He turns away from her, resting his hand on the head of his dog, his wise mentor. No harm will come to this young man.

151897.title: Willem van der Helm (c 1625-75), Municipal Architect of Leiden, with his Wife Belytgen Cornelisdr van der Schelt (d 1661) and their Son Leendert (1622-64)
151897.creator: Barent Fabritius

editorial.note: Barent Fabritius (1624 - 1673). The architect Willem van der Helm of Leiden (c. 1625 - 1675) with his wife and son, 1656.
The Bible recounts how Jacob, pretending to be his brother Esau, tricked their blind father into bestowing Esau’s rightful blessing on him.

This woman, engaged in handiwork, ponders a romantic proposition. She looks thoughtfully at the bird presented to her by a hopeful hunter. In the 17th century, ‘birding’ was a euphemism for making love.

Cornelis Kruseman was sometimes called ‘Italian Kruseman’ owing to his love for Italian art. After spending time in Rome (1821-1825), he worked in the Netherlands in the idealized style that he knew from Italy.
In 1821 Kruseman travelled to Italy. According to this picture’s inscription, he painted it in Rome. It combines both Dutch and Italian painting traditions.

152056.title: Interior with a Woman Feeding a Parrot, Known as ‘The Parrot Cage’
152056.creator: Jan Havicksz. Steen

editorial.note: This scene bursts with life. On the left, a woman is frying oysters, while a mischievous boy tries to feed a cat. On the right, two men are playing a game of trictrac (a kind of backgammon).

A man and woman are so drunk that they are unaware they are being robbed. Their foolishness is underscored by the print on the partition. It depicts an owl, considered a stupid creature in the 17th century.

Faint from fever, the young woman rests her head on a pillow. Is she perhaps lovesick? Is she pregnant? To find out, a quack would put a strip of his patient’s clothing in a brazier to smoulder – the scent would disclose her secret.

152080.title: Old Woman Saying Grace, Known as ‘The Prayer without End’
152080.creator: Nicolaes Maes

editorial.note: An old woman prays devoutly before eating her meal. She does not let the begging cat tugging impatiently on the tablecloth distract her. The virtue of the old woman lies in her self-control and sense of duty to God.

152120.title: Interior with a Mother Combing Her Child’s Hair, Known as ‘Maternal Care’
152120.creator: Caspar Netscher

editorial.note: These two children serve as examples of good and bad upbringing. Toys litter the floor in a dimly lit bedroom. A mother combs the long curls of her son, who obediently leans on her lap.
Domenico Maggiotto (1713 - 1794). Girl with a Fruitbasket, c. 1760 - 1765. Bequest of J.W. Edwin vom Rath, 1941.

On their way to Emmaus, two Disciples unexpectedly encounter Christ. At first they do not recognise him. As they sit to eat and they break bread, they realise who he is. And at that moment, he disappears.

152358.title: Man and Woman at the Breakfast Table

editorial.note: On the table is a plate with a ham, cheese, and bread. For the average family, this was a typical breakfast, sometimes supplemented by fish. The woman is about to pour some beer into her flute glass.
The feast of St Nicholas takes place in December. In the Netherlands, it has been celebrated in the same way for centuries. Good children receive gifts from the saint.
